root_cause: Several MSVC link.exe invocations ran concurrently (ninja/cmake parallel build) on the Windows CC runner and collectively exhausted available memory, causing link.exe to abort with LNK1102 (out of memory) for six separate link targets within the same ~30-second window. This is the same recurring infrastructure-level resource exhaustion pattern already tracked under signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e (24 prior occurrences since 2026-11-03), not a regression introduced by the triggering commit e8f95c0862b5425b9efadb5f367bf71f43aced0b (PR #40056, a small CPU/ARM rounding fix unrelated to build parallelism or link targets).
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally; it depends on Windows runner memory pressure during a Release build with the full set of conformance/test/sample targets linked in parallel. Can be approximated by running `cmake --build . --config Release -j <max-parallel>` on a memory-constrained Windows machine while building ov_subgraphs_dumper_tests, sync_benchmark, ov_api_conformance_tests, ov_op_conformance_tests, ov_subgraphs_dumper and _pyopenvino concurrently.
recommended_actions: Reduce the link-stage parallelism (e.g., cap ninja/cmake -j for the Windows CC job, or set CMAKE_JOB_POOLS to limit concurrent linker invocations) to avoid simultaneous LINK.exe out-of-memory failures.
Consider enabling /DEBUG:FASTLINK or disabling LTCG/incremental PDB generation for conformance/test executables that do not need full debug info, to reduce per-link memory footprint.
Evaluate moving to a larger-memory Windows runner SKU for the Windows Conditional Compilation workflow given 24+ recorded occurrences of this infrastructure pattern in the last 3 weeks.
File/escalate an infra ticket referencing signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e given its high recurrence count so the CI infra owners can address runner sizing or build parallelism configuration.
prevention_strategies: Limit the number of concurrent link.exe processes on memory-constrained Windows CI runners (via build-system job pools or -j flags), and monitor runner memory headroom for the Windows CC workflow. Since this is a known, frequently recurring infra issue, consider adding automatic retry-on-LNK1102 logic or runner size increase rather than relying on manual re-triage for each occurrence.
historical_context: This exact signature (Windows Release build out-of-memory during compile/link under high parallelism, LNK1102) has been recorded 24 times since 2026-11-03, most recently a few hours before this run (2026-11-24T11:33:31Z). It is an established recurring infrastructure pattern unrelated to specific commits; affected_commits in the pattern record span many unrelated PRs, confirming it is parallelism/runner-memory driven rather than code-related.
